```{r setup, include = FALSE}
has_deps <- requireNamespace("causaldata", quietly = TRUE) &&
            requireNamespace("SuperLearner", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  eval = has_deps, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.6, fig.align = "center"
)
library(dr3)
```

`dr3` implements the average treatment effect (ATE) estimators reconciled in
*Three Routes to One Answer*. The organizing idea is that AIPW, TMLE, and double
machine learning all target the **same** efficient influence function

$$
D(O) = \Big[\tfrac{A}{g(X)} - \tfrac{1-A}{1-g(X)}\Big]\,\big(Y - Q_A(X)\big)
       + \big(Q_1(X) - Q_0(X)\big) - \psi,
$$

and differ only in **how they solve it** (average the score vs. targeting) and
**how the nuisances** $g(X)=P(A=1\mid X)$ and $Q_a(X)=E[Y\mid A=a,X]$ are fit
(full-sample, cross-fit, or double cross-fit). `dr3` runs the whole family on one
shared Super Learner library, so the differences you see come from the
combination rule and the fitting scheme (and, for split-based estimators, from
the random split), not from separate implementations.

```{r note, echo = FALSE, results = "asis", eval = !has_deps}
cat("> This vignette needs the suggested packages **causaldata** and",
    "**SuperLearner**; its code is shown but not run here.\n")
```

## One call

We use the canonical Hernán–Robins NHEFS example (quitting smoking → 1971–1982
weight change), which ships in `causaldata`, so nothing needs downloading.

```{r panel}
d <- dr_nhefs()

# A small library keeps the vignette fast; use default_dr_library for real work.
set.seed(1)   # the full-sample fits use the current RNG state; `seed` sets the folds
fit <- dr_panel(d$Y, d$A, d$X, SL.library = c("SL.mean", "SL.glm", "SL.glmnet"),
                seed = 1)
fit
```

```{r spread, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
dr6 <- fit$estimate[!fit$estimator %in% c("g-computation", "IPTW")]
cat(sprintf(paste(
  "In this single run the six doubly-robust estimates (AIPW, TMLE, DML, CV-TMLE, DC-AIPW,",
  "DC-TMLE) span %.2f kg, from %.2f to %.2f kg; the singly-robust plug-ins (g-computation,",
  "IPTW) carry no analytic interval. One split with a small library is noisy: the paper",
  "repeats the split 100 times with a larger library and reports medians, and there the six",
  "estimates span 0.07 kg (its Steps 4 and 5)."),
  diff(range(dr6)), min(dr6), max(dr6)))
```

## Plot it

```{r forest}
plot(fit)
```

## Look under the hood

`dr_panel()` is a thin wrapper. You can fit the shared nuisances yourself and
hand them to any estimator — pairing `dr_aipw()` with cross-fit nuisances *is*
double machine learning:

```{r nuisance}
nu <- dr_nuisance(d$Y, d$A, d$X, strategy = "crossfit",
                  SL.library = c("SL.mean", "SL.glm", "SL.glmnet"))
dr_aipw(d$Y, d$A, nu)$estimate   # DML
dr_tmle(d$Y, d$A, nu)$estimate   # CV-TMLE
```
